newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl affirms EMU goals, timetable - Berlusconi.
newsitem.headline: Kohl affirms EMU goals, timetable - Berlusconi.

text.p: Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Thursday after meeting Chancellor Helmut Kohl that the German leader had made clear to him the timetable and criteria for European monetary union (EMU) would be adhered to.

"The chancellor reconfirmed that the drive for European union continues. The Maastricht Treaty will be adhered to in terms of meeting the criteria and the timetable," the former Italian prime minister told a news conference.
Asked if Kohl had assured him Italy could take part in EMU from the start it if met the criteria, Berlusconi said: "I didn't ask the chancellor that question. He could not have given me an answer."
He added: "The answer will be given by the conference of the member states of the European Union next spring, looking at the data for the individual countries in 1997."

Berlusconi, who leads the centre-right Forza Italia party, said he personally hoped the currency union would be as large as possible. He also said all major parties in Italy were ready to make a contribution to make sure the country qualifies.

"It would be very serious if the single currency is not the currency of all European countries," he said. "This is why it was created, because a real single market can be realised via the single currency."
Berlusconi also said Kohl, widely seen as the driving force behind European integration, remained as committed as ever to the cause.
